newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders cited, Guatemala features.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders cited, Guatemala features.

text.p: Guatemala was in the limelight of Wednesday's new business on the sugar freight market, shipbrokers said.
London-based trade house E D & F Man issued two new orders for vessels to ship cargoes from Puerto Quetzal.
It quoted for 25,000 tonnes in bulk from both the port and Acajutla to Casablanca plus various options for April 15/20 and a further 16,000 in bags to Colombo.

C.Czarnikow was open for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to south China for 10 days notice and Genoc for 25/33,000 tonnes from Cuba to Egyptian Mediterranean, Black Sea or Baltic for the end of April.
The only other new inquiry to emerge was a small 3,000-tonne bagged parcel from Louis Dreyfus from Puerto Quetzal to Chile for prompt shipment.
Of the day's reported firmer business, shipbrokers said Tate & Lyle was closely working its recent order for 18,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Barbados to London for mid-April.
Cargill fixed a prompt 14,000-tonne cargo of bagged sugar from north Continent to Lagos. The rate has yet to be reported.
In other news, Iran was reported to have bought at least one cargo of white sugar for May 15/June 15 shipment dates.
